findings.counterargument: The original CLI normally constructs sandboxed attempts; the vulnerability matters when importing or constructing manifests.
findings.impact: A caller can claim sandboxed verification without isolation; the original status derivation ignores the sandboxed flag.
findings.recommended_action: Reject passed attempts with sandboxed=false and verify the regression with a zero-exit unsandboxed attempt.
findings.title: Unsandboxed zero-exit attempt counts as passed

findings.counterargument: Normal capture populates metadata; existing validators admit externally supplied incomplete artifacts.
findings.impact: A manifest can omit hashes and sizes, so changed output can be treated as verified evidence.
findings.recommended_action: Require SHA-256 and size metadata for verification and test missing metadata and post-capture tampering.
findings.title: Artifact verification accepts absent integrity metadata

findings.counterargument: Strict JSON loading rejects inconsistent manifest status, reducing exposure through the existing validate-findings CLI.
findings.impact: Reports can endorse a no-edit decision without recorded required attempts if constructed models bypass the JSON loader.
findings.recommended_action: Derive the decision from required attempts and clean discovery, then test an asserted pass with no attempts.
findings.title: No-edit decision trusts an asserted pass without checks
